background_notes.fact: For a,b,d≥0 with d²=a²+b² and m=max(a,b), one has m≤d≤√2·m. Here √2 is finite nonnegative and (√2)²=2.

grounds.reason: a and b are respectively a Euclidean norm and an absolute value; d is the Euclidean target distance, and the displayed finite-sum computation establishes d²=a²+b².
The norm is the nonnegative square root of the finite sum of coordinate squares.

background_notes.justification: Since 0≤a,b≤m and m is one of a,b, m²≤a²+b²≤2m²=(√2·m)². Squaring preserves and reflects order between nonnegative reals: if 0≤x<y then y²−x²=(y−x)(y+x)>0. Apply this to the two inequalities. These are exactly the square-root and sign conditions used in S001.

background_notes.fact: If (Z,d) is a metric space, then d_max((x,t),(y,u))=max(d(x,y),|t−u|) is a metric on Z×ℝ; its finite distances canonically define an extended metric. Thus MaxProd(Ambient n) and Ambient(n+1) satisfy the space hypotheses of M006/M007 for every n≥0.

grounds.reason: Ambient m is the specified Euclidean inner product space with its norm distance, for all natural m including zero.
MaxProd uses exactly the maximum of the given metric distance and real absolute difference.

background_notes.justification: Nonnegativity and symmetry follow for each component. A zero maximum forces both component distances to vanish, hence equality of both coordinates. Each component distance across three points is at most the sum of the corresponding two component distances, which is at most the sum of the two maxima; taking the maximum proves the triangle inequality. Embedding nonnegative finite distances into [0,∞] preserves these metric axioms. No dimension or nonemptiness condition is introduced.
